svg.title: Assume each experiment begins with an independently trusted seed S ∈{1, . . . , m}, with known fixed weights ws > 0, ∑︁ s ws = 1. The validator observes S and Y after the complete experiment. It neither selects a seed retrospectively nor discards an inconvenient seed. Deployment uses the same seed law. The seed weights hold conditional on the completed validation past and selected label; completed experiments use the declared fresh stock. Thus the following likelihood and drift statements are conditional on the common proof filtration, without giving the reader access to the hidden preparation label. For one label, nominate a good conditional-error vector ps ∈(0, 1) with ̄p = ∑︁ s wsps < ε < 1. The bad class consists of all conditional risks qs whose average exceeds ε, with no hidden response-model constraint.
